page: Amazon Web Services c7gn.2xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the 64-bit arm64 architecture. The server provides 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs running AWS Neoverse-V1 processors clocked at 2.6 GHz with a single thread per core. Memory capacity totals 16.0 GB, establishing a 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio. Cache architecture consists of 64 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. The instance provisions no integrated local storage and no GPU accelerators, relying on remote EBS volumes for persistent storage. Network capability is highlighted by a high baseline bandwidth of 25 Gbps.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent compute and network-oriented throughput. The platform recorded a Geekbench multi-core score of 8,436.0, a single-core score of 1,524.0, and achieved 11,938.0 in clang software compilation tasks. Memory subsystems reached 150.89 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 67.61 GB/sec for write operations. Workload throughput tests yielded 13.54 million operations per second on Redis SET benchmarks and 16.28 GB/sec in static web serving. Conversely, PassMark CPU testing scored 6,153.63, with encryption reaching 1,105.51, and prompt processing for a 7B parameter LLM measured at 15.04 tokens per second, reflecting architectural tradeoffs in dense cryptography and complex matrix inference.

With its 1:2 memory-to-vCPU allocation, dedicated execution cores, and 25 Gbps network interface, the c7gn.2xlarge is suited for network-intensive compute tasks, web serving, in-memory caching systems, and arm64-targeted software build pipelines.

It features 16.0 GB of memory, providing a 2.0 GB per core ratio, along with a 25 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The instance includes no attached local storage and no GPU accelerators. Benchmark evaluations show solid performance across general compute tasks, registering 8,436.0 on Geekbench multi-core, 11,938.0 on clang compilation, and 13.54 million operations per second in Redis SET operations. Memory throughput achieves 150.89 GB/sec on uncached reads. Tradeoffs appear in lower PassMark encryption scores and limited performance in larger language model inference. The configuration suits network-heavy compute jobs, static web delivery, caching tiers, and CI/CD build environments.
